gates.normative_summary: Signed clean install, Finder selection. The service is discoverable through the supported Services route and opens the selected draft.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later, signed and notarised installed companion with an OS-registered Finder Service. arm64 is the only architecture this checkout builds for.

evidence.covers: Writes the NSServices declaration into the generated Info.plist, so the Services route exists as a packaged declaration.
Pins the packaged bundle identity and asserts the manifest records the candidate as unsigned and not release eligible.

gates.missing_condition: No signed or notarised build exists. The packaging script emits candidate_status qualification_only, signature_status unsigned and production_release_eligible false, and no codesign, spctl, notarytool or stapler invocation exists anywhere in the repository, so macOS has never registered this Services entry.
gates.limitations: The only evidence is that the Services declaration is written into a plist on disk. Writing a declaration is not discovery: nothing shows the Services menu item appearing, nor a draft opening from a real Finder selection.

gates.normative_summary: Services invoked while the companion is closed. The provider starts through supported OS behaviour, and no Core mutation occurs before Add.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later, signed installed companion, cold process. Covers the Services activation path only.

evidence.covers: An unready companion admits no selection from any surface, so the advertised route cannot open a draft it cannot serve.
Adoption of a durable request mutates neither queue nor subscription, which is the no-mutation-before-Add rule on the Share route rather than the Services route.

gates.missing_condition: Cold activation of the Services provider by launchd requires an installed, signed companion that macOS has registered. No test launches the companion process from a Services invocation, and the no-mutation rule is demonstrated only on the Share route.
gates.limitations: Both references are in-process unit tests in an unsigned swift test binary. Neither starts a process, and neither exercises NSApp.servicesProvider.

gates.normative_summary: Programmatic Services invocation. The same explicit Add boundary applies, with bounded validation.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later, signed installed companion. Covers programmatic callers of the registered Services route.

evidence.covers: Each intake surface carries its own provenance through review, so a programmatic caller cannot borrow another surface's boundary.
The bounded validation that applies uniformly to every surface, including a programmatic one.

gates.missing_condition: A programmatic Services invocation can only be made against a build macOS has registered. No harness exists that calls the registered service from outside the process.
gates.limitations: The boundary and the bound are proven as pure policy values. Nothing drives them from an external caller.

gates.normative_summary: Multi-file picker and drop. Both routes produce the same typed items, the same count, the same destination and the same payload behaviour.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later, signed installed companion. Covers the NSOpenPanel pickers and the status-item drop route.

evidence.covers: The fixed file-picker policy: many files, no directory.
The fixed folder-picker policy, so the two pickers cannot drift into each other.
The drop route carries the same selection bound as the picker route.

gates.missing_condition: No real NSOpenPanel is ever presented and no real drag session is ever performed. Both policies are asserted as values, so the gate's requirement that the two routes agree in practice is untested.
gates.limitations: Policy equality is checked, not route equality. The drop view and the panel controller have no tests at all.

gates.normative_summary: Paste a note, then drop files. The note survives, and there is no silent mode or destination change.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion capture draft holding a typed note and subsequently dropped files.

evidence.covers: Dropped text becomes a reviewed captured copy, which is how a note is represented once it is submitted.
A typed note, the keep-updated mode and the destination are each asserted unchanged after two files are dropped into the same draft through CapturePanelController.addIncoming.
The same three survive incoming work rebuilding the panel chrome, which is the path the note-and-mode reset lived on.

gates.limitations: The drop runs through the real draft and the real panel controller. The note is set through a test accessor on the panel's own text view rather than a real paste, and the destination is an immutable workspaceName, so that clause is structural rather than observed. The one test that reaches buildWindow, where the reset lived, is skipped when NSScreen.screens is empty, so a headless runner proves the gate only on the window-less path.

gates.normative_summary: An incoming Finder request arrives during an unsent draft. The existing draft is retained, and the incoming selection is reviewed separately with its own destination and its own Add.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later, signed installed companion with a registered Finder Service, holding an unsent draft.

evidence.covers: A second selection from the Shortcuts route waits behind the one under review rather than merging into it.
The same waiting-selection behaviour on the durable Share route.
Separate confirmation and receipt per reviewed group, which is the own-destination-and-own-Add half of the requirement.

gates.missing_condition: The gate names the Finder Service specifically, which requires an installed signed build macOS has registered. The waiting-selection behaviour is proven on the Shortcuts and Share routes only.
gates.limitations: Route-equivalence is assumed from shared code, not demonstrated. No test drives the Finder Service into a live draft.

gates.normative_summary: Escape, reopen and quit while a draft exists. A running draft is restored, quit semantics are explicit, and there is no unpromised crash persistence.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later, installed companion with a live capture panel and a draft in progress.

evidence.covers: Quit releases candidates that never reached review and refuses new requests, which is the explicit quit semantics.
Restart restores only unconfirmed groups, which bounds what persistence is promised.

gates.missing_condition: Escape handling and window lifecycle live in CapturePanelController, which has no tests and cannot be exercised without a real window server session on an installed build.
gates.limitations: Quit and restart are exercised as store-level operations. No keypress, no panel dismissal and no reopen is performed anywhere.

gates.normative_summary: An unsupported, oversized or mixed selection. Invalid rows remain listed, and nothing is silently omitted or truncated.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion review draft, every intake surface. The policy is platform-independent Swift exercised on the macOS CI row.

evidence.covers: A refused row stays listed and blocks submission until removed, which is the invalid-rows-remain requirement.
A mixed selection is classified item by item in the supplied order, so no member is dropped.
A selection already holding grants is refused whole rather than partly retained, which is the no-silent-omission requirement.
Unsupported, duplicate and over-bound members are each refused at the draft.
The oversized case specifically: a per-format size bound refuses the member rather than truncating it.
Per-item and whole-selection byte bounds refuse before any staging, on the drop route.

gates.limitations: Unit level, in an unsigned swift test process on the macos-latest CI runner whose OS and Xcode versions are not recorded. Selections are constructed in-test rather than arriving from a real picker, drag or Services invocation, and the refusal reasons are checked as policy values rather than as rendered rows.

gates.normative_summary: An exact UTF-8, BOM and line-ending fixture. The bytes Core preserves match the selected source. Section 20 additionally requires that source bytes and relevant filesystem attributes be compared before and after ingestion.
gates.applicability: Every qualified text source on every OS the Core runtime supports, plus the macOS companion capture path that selects it.

evidence.covers: A BOM and the source line endings survive extraction unchanged.
The read path returns the exact bytes and their digest.
Unicode names and exact case survive the read.
The companion publishes a prepared selection with frozen bytes.
The committed UTF-8, BOM and CRLF/LF/lone-CR fixture has its SHA-256 recorded beside it, as section 20 requires of fixture hashes.
The fixture is the recorded one: digest, leading BOM, two CRLF, one lone CR, two lone LF and no terminator.
Drives the Swift half against a managed Core, then reads the retained copy and the extraction projection back out of the Core workspace and compares both to the recorded digest and bytes.

The selected original goes through ManualCaptureSubmission, the frozen payload equals the fixture, CaptureDeliveryCoordinator over CLICaptureDelivery admits it through the real omnivia CLI, and the original's bytes, size, mode, owner, inode, flags, mtime/birthtime/ctime, extended attributes, sibling listing and directory mtime are identical before and after.

gates.limitations: Executed and passing on macOS with a Swift toolchain on 2026-10-16. The end-to-end half is a macOS-only pytest that runs `swift test`; it skips elsewhere, so core-acceptance's Linux row runs only the fixture-digest and extraction tests, and no required CI row runs the end-to-end half. The original is chosen by handing its URL to ManualCaptureSubmission rather than through a real picker, drag or Services invocation, and atime is deliberately excluded from the before-and-after comparison because a read may move it. Core's retained copy is read through read_retained_source against the stopped service's workspace rather than over the wire. One text fixture covers the gate; no OS or Xcode version is recorded with the result.

gates.normative_summary: A pasted path, an embedded URL and instruction text. Each is stored as inert content, with no arbitrary file read, no fetch and no execution.
gates.applicability: Every intake surface on macOS 13 or later, and the Core extraction path for every qualified format.

evidence.covers: An embedded URL is classified as an inert link rather than a retrievable reference.
The link is adopted as its own text and nothing is fetched.
Instruction text is adopted verbatim and acted on in no way.
No reference in an extracted document causes an outbound action.
Formula-like strings stay values and nothing is evaluated.
The Share extension carries no network entitlement, which makes the no-fetch rule structural rather than a promise.
A shared filesystem path is adopted as its own text through the real Share inbox: the named file's own bytes never appear in the adopted snapshot.
A path left in the review note adopts nothing, queues nothing and connects no access grant, so nothing opens it.

gates.limitations: The URL and instruction-text halves run on the real Share adoption path. The pasted-path half is proven by absence: the named file's bytes do not reach the adopted snapshot, and no grant, queue entry or subscription appears. Nothing spies on file opens, the note is set through a test accessor rather than a real paste, and Extensions/Share's own view controller is outside the Swift test target.

gates.normative_summary: A known eligible local target while offline. An explicit Add publishes a durable local snapshot, with accurate queue wording.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion with no network, against a target whose eligibility policy is already approved.

evidence.covers: An explicit manual submission publishes frozen bytes into the durable queue.
The queue persists the exact intent and payload, which is the durability half.
A published durable request is complete and readable without the companion running.
An explicit Add with nothing to deliver to publishes the frozen payload durably and reports queued only, never Added and never naming the destination.
ShareInboxStore.queuedWording is the design's exact sentence, and the published manifest on disk names no destination, workspace, target or principal.

The production panel receipt for a single Add reads Queued on this Mac., and a delivery pass through the real CLI against an installation that is not there leaves the item pending with its exact bytes and the activity label Queued on this Mac.

A real installed, initialised Core started and then stopped with the CLI's own service commands. An explicit Add through the production panel and queue reads Queued on this Mac. A delivery pass through the real CLI sends nothing, leaves the service stopped (service status afterwards is status_not_running), keeps the item pending with the frozen intent and exact bytes, survives a companion restart and a second pass, and shows Queued on this Mac. After Start Core the same frozen item is admitted. Disabling the gate makes the CLI start Core and admit it, and the test fails.

The status gate passes against a real running Core, then a wrapper stops that Core as the production capture command is launched. The capture, run with --require-running, is refused as not sent: the item stays pending with one known-no-effect attempt and service status afterwards is status_not_running. Removing --require-running makes the capture start Core and the test fails.
The production capture invocation carries --require-running ahead of the command and is otherwise unchanged.

With --require-running an absent descriptor or a dead endpoint exits 1 with the fixed not-running sentence, writes nothing to stdout and never reaches connect_managed_local, which the test makes raise if called.

The pre-send gate reads the CLI's redacted service status document and sends only to a running service whose target and workspace are the frozen ones; another target, another workspace or a missing safe status is not sent to.
A stopped, unreachable, internal-error, unreadable or wrong-action status fails closed to not sent; an incompatible one holds the item (AT-12).
The companion's frozen target reference equals the CLI's own, computed with realpath, which the gate compares against.
The Share extension source assigns ShareInboxStore.queuedWording to its status in both queued states and never assigns Added.

gates.limitations: Executed and passing against a real installation on 2026-10-16. Offline is a deliberately stopped local service, the only offline a local unix-socket Core has; the host network is not disabled. The status gate classifies target and compatibility; the send runs the CLI with --require-running, which attaches through ServiceClient.connect and never reaches the managed launcher, so a Core stopped between the gate and the capture is refused as not sent and left stopped (the race test stops the real Core as the capture is launched; removing the flag fails it). The closed-companion sentence is the Share extension's, pinned by source text because Extensions/Share is outside the Swift test target. The real-installation tests skip, naming OMNIVIA_CORE_TEST_PYTHON or the missing omnivia-core-service, when the toolchain is absent. One text item and one workspace; eligibility is frozen target and workspace identity only.

gates.normative_summary: A missing, revoked or incompatible target. There is no silent fallback, and the intended input is retained appropriately.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion delivering to a Core target, every delivery route.

evidence.covers: A mismatched target is not delivered to, so there is no fallback target.
An out-of-date target binding revision refuses delivery, which is the incompatible-target case.
A mismatched workspace refuses delivery rather than redirecting.
A definite failure retains the recovery payload across restart, which is the input-retained half.
A target whose executable is gone fails to launch and is reported as not sent.
The real CLI against an absent installation returns the item to pending with its bytes and an unchanged frozen intent on every pass, and a present target with a different binding is handed nothing.
The queued bytes survive a queue restart while the target is absent.
The sentences the companion matches are the CLI source's own.
The CLI's credential and version refusals classify as holds (Needs access, Update required), and every other shape stays unknown.
Service refusals about access or version hold the item, an outcome the runtime could not establish stays unknown, and any other refusal is still a definite failure.

Through the coordinator a refused credential or version leaves the original item pending and held, with its bytes, frozen intent, settled attempt and key intact across a restart, no later pass or restart sends it, and the activity says Needs access or Update required with no reason code.

A target that now accepts the credential is handed nothing until the hold is explicitly released, the wrong reason releases nothing, and release lets the next pass send under the next attempt's own key.
An absent target stays known-no-effect and plain pending with no hold.
A hold settles the refused attempt as known-no-effect and keeps the payload and operation key across a restart.
A held item starts no attempt, release needs the matching reason, and the next attempt uses the next generation's key.
Only the exact active attempt can be held, never an unknown-outcome one.
A tampered hold is refused without rewriting, a held manifest carries its own schema so an older build refuses it, and releasing writes the ordinary schema.

gates.missing_condition: Absent is observed through the real CLI, and revoked and incompatible now hold the original pending intent as Needs access or Update required, durably, with bytes, frozen intent, attempt history and key kept and nothing resent, retargeted or failed. Two named conditions are still not exercised through the production path: no test has a real revoked credential or a real version disagreement produce the refusal through the companion (the tests hand the CLI's fixed stderr sentence, exit status and service error codes to CLICaptureDelivery.outcome and pin the sentences against the CLI source), and CaptureDeliveryCoordinator.releaseHeld has no production caller, because no companion access or update flow exists yet to release a hold, so explicit release is exercised only by tests. The design's Access to this workspace is required wording for a revoked authorisation is also not shown; the panel says Needs access.
gates.limitations: The no-silent-fallback property is strong and includes an absent target through the real CLI. A held item is queue-resolvable, so unlike the old failed arm its bytes are recoverable through the queue, and release starts the next generation under a new key, which is correct only because the refused attempt is settled as known-no-effect. Two tests that drive the real CLI skip without OMNIVIA_CORE_TEST_PYTHON. Delivery elsewhere in the older coordinator tests still uses a fake client.

gates.normative_summary: The principal or the target profile changes before the first send or during recovery, including a cached Share. A frozen original intent pauses; there is no redirected delivery and no replay under the new account.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion holding an unsent or recovering intent, across the manual, Share and automatic routes.

evidence.covers: The frozen caller binding must match at publication, so a changed caller cannot publish the old intent.
A mismatched caller context refuses delivery rather than redirecting it.
The cached Share request carries no principal, destination or workspace, so there is nothing for a new account to inherit.

gates.missing_condition: No test changes the signed-in principal or the target profile and then asserts the frozen intent enters a paused state. The refusals prove no redirection, but a refusal is not the pause the gate requires, and the recovery variant is not covered at all.
gates.limitations: Caller and workspace identity are compared as opaque values supplied by the test. No real authentication boundary participates.

gates.normative_summary: A provider URL expires as the callback returns. The extension-owned complete copy survives and is the only payload used.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later, signed installed Share extension receiving provider-backed representations.

evidence.covers: Adopted copies survive removal of the source, which is the owned-copy-is-the-only-payload rule.
A provider file URL is copied rather than bookmarked, so expiry cannot invalidate the payload.

gates.missing_condition: A real NSItemProvider whose URL expires mid-callback only occurs inside a Share extension macOS has loaded. The Extensions tree is outside the Swift test target, has no tests, and is not even typechecked in CI.
gates.limitations: Copy-not-bookmark and survival-after-source-removal are proven against a test-owned temporary file. No provider, no expiry and no extension process are involved.

gates.normative_summary: Share with inPlace false and inPlace true. Both are handled correctly, and neither automatically grants companion-owned original access.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later, signed installed Share extension, both in-place variants.

evidence.covers: Both the data and URL variants remain snapshots, so neither becomes a durable original.
Adoption grants no subscription, so a share cannot become a watched original.
A snapshot cannot be put under Keep updated, which is the no-automatic-original-access rule.

gates.missing_condition: The design states inPlace is never requested, which can only be confirmed against the real NSExtensionItem configuration macOS hands a loaded Share extension. No test reads an inPlace flag, because no test runs the extension.
gates.limitations: The no-original-access invariant is proven on the companion side. The two inPlace variants themselves are never distinguished by any test.

gates.normative_summary: Extension termination before or after publication. Before: no queued acknowledgement. After: the original submitted intent resumes.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion and Share extension sharing the App Group spool.

evidence.covers: A staged request is invisible until the atomic publish, so termination before publication leaves nothing to acknowledge.
An unpublished request is never adopted.
A request published while the companion was closed resumes at startup.
Startup reconciliation clears only staging no live writer can still own.

gates.missing_condition: Termination is modelled by abandoning a staging directory in-process. No test kills a real extension process, so the crash-safety of the atomic rename is argued from the code path rather than observed under a real signal.
gates.limitations: Both halves are covered behaviourally against a temporary directory standing in for the App Group container. No App Group is registered and no second process participates.

gates.normative_summary: Companion termination during publication. Recovery yields either a complete published submission or a cleanly confirmed abandoned candidate, and never a false complete queue.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion publishing into the durable intent queue.

evidence.covers: A failure before publication leaves nothing and the candidate is cleaned at restart.
An interrupted stage becomes an explicit unknown rather than a false complete.
A completion failure after publication leaves the entry recoverable and the replay does not duplicate it.
A lost index acknowledgement recovers the whole batch rather than part of it.

gates.missing_condition: Termination is simulated by injected write failures and by reopening the store, never by terminating the process. The design's durability barriers, specifically the parent-directory fsync before an acknowledged rename, are not verified against a real interruption.
gates.limitations: The recovery state machine is covered thoroughly. What is not covered is that the on-disk ordering survives a real kill or power loss, which is the part the gate is actually about.

gates.normative_summary: A crash after the Core commit but before the local receipt. Same-key reconciliation produces one canonical effect.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion against a live Core service. Spans the companion queue and the Core admission boundary.

evidence.covers: An uncertain delivery preserves the recovery identity, so reconciliation uses the same key.
On the Core side an exact replay of the same key produces one canonical effect.
A replay whose body changed is refused without a domain effect.

The real durable queue, wire encoder and CLICaptureDelivery deliver to a live omnivia-core-service; the receipt is dropped after Core commits, the queue is reopened from disk, the restarted coordinator replays the frozen request under the retained attempt key and settles the entry on the admitted answer, and Core history still holds exactly one capture with that id.
Control: the same lost receipt reconciled under a different key yields two captures, so the one-capture assertion can see a duplicate.
The production coordinator replays an unknown entry on its own key and generation, and settles it only on an admitted answer.

gates.limitations: Executed and passing against a live service on 2026-10-16. The crash is simulated by dropping the receipt after the CLI returns and reopening the queue over the same root, not by killing a process mid-flight. The two Core boundary tests skip when omnivia and omnivia-core-service are not installed side by side on PATH, and fail instead when CI is set, so a row that lost the toolchain cannot go green. One text item, one document and one workspace; a lost receipt after a multi-item batch is not covered.

gates.normative_summary: A timeout, an expired replay or an unknown admission. The state shown is Checking status, with no destructive removal and no new-key resubmission.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion recovering an in-flight submission, and the Core admission boundary it reconciles against.

evidence.covers: An unknown outcome cannot be resubmitted under a new key without conclusive no-effect evidence.
A timeout preserves the recovery identity rather than discarding the attempt.
An expired replay is refused rather than silently re-run.
An unknown delivery outcome projects through the production CaptureActivityStore and FilesAndFoldersModel to the Checking status label, with the activity record preserved rather than cleared.
A Core refusal carrying outcome_established false is read as an unknown outcome, not a definite failure.
An ordinary idempotency conflict, which proves the request never committed, stays a definite failure.
The outcome_established false detail reaches the wire in the error envelope.
A refused replay leaves the entry unknown with its key and bytes and settles nothing.
Repeated unknown replays all use the one retained key and never allocate another.

The timeout arm through the production CLICaptureDelivery's own deadline, shortened via processDeadline. A real executable passes the status gate, then never answers the capture; the delivery ends it and returns unknown. The queue keeps the entry unknown with its attempt key, generation, intent and exact bytes; a second pass reuses the key. The production CaptureActivityStore and FilesAndFoldersModel show Checking status… with no receipt, and Clear completed activity removes nothing. Dropping the deadline, reporting not-sent, or not terminating fails it.
A CLICaptureDelivery nobody configured waits exactly 25 seconds; the CLI --timeout-ms 20000 is pinned beside it in testTheCaptureCommandAttachesOnlyAndNeverStartsCore.

Expired replay and unknown admission, end to end. A live omnivia-core-service commits a real capture and the receipt is lost; with the service stopped, a test-only helper re-stores the claim's answer non-canonically; the real omnivia CLI's replay returns Core's own outcome_established false. Through the production queue and coordinator, two passes stay unknown under the same key and generation with exact bytes, show Checking status…, survive Clear completed activity, and Core holds one capture. A pre-tamper control is admitted; ignoring outcome_established or skipping the tamper fails it.

gates.limitations: Executed and passing on 2026-10-16. Expired replay means a committed claim whose answer Core cannot re-serve; claims do not expire in this build, and a test-only helper builds that state by editing the stored outcome with the service stopped. The timeout arm's status read is a recorded running-Core document served by a wrapper; the capture process, deadline and termination are real, but the timeout is not driven against a live Core. The live arm skips without a configured Python, and fails if CI is set and python3 cannot run it. Displayed state is the production projection, not a rendered view. The folder window's reprocess Checking status sentences belong to a different operation than this gate's in-flight submission and are untested, as is Stop adding remaining files against a Checking folder member.

gates.normative_summary: A native queue capacity race across the Share and manual routes. Count and byte reservations never exceed feature-controlled limits.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion and Share extension contending for the same native-owned quota, on the macOS CI row.

evidence.covers: Concurrent writers never overshoot the quota, which is the race the gate names.
In-flight staging reserves its worst case, so a reservation cannot be double-spent.
The count limit holds.
The byte limit counts both published and candidate bytes on the manual route.
Owned-copy quotas still bind on the handoff route, so no route escapes the limit.

gates.limitations: Unsigned swift test process on the macos-latest runner, whose OS and Xcode versions are not recorded. Concurrency is real threads against a temporary directory standing in for the App Group container, with an in-process plus flock cross-process lock; two genuinely separate signed processes are never raced, and the limits themselves are the build's own constants rather than values a feature flag supplied.

gates.normative_summary: A symlink, a tampered manifest or a tampered payload. Each is rejected, and sent outcomes are reconciled without altered replay.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion and Share extension, every staging and publication store, on the macOS CI row.

evidence.covers: A manifest that does not match its bytes is refused at publication.
A tampered payload of the right length is still refused.
Tampered bytes are dropped rather than retried forever.
A planted file at the owned name is replaced, never reused.
A tampered published batch fails closed.
A sent outcome reconciles through exact replay while a conflicting replay is refused, which is the no-altered-replay requirement.
A delivered promise must be a contained regular file, so a symlink is refused rather than followed.
The owned-copy store refuses traversal in a staged name.

gates.limitations: Unsigned swift test process on the macos-latest runner, with OS and Xcode versions unrecorded. Tampering is performed in-process on temporary directories, and the symlink refusals rest on lstat checks exercised against test-created links rather than against a hostile provider. The manifest schemas involved are this build's own, so a cross-version tampered manifest is not covered here.

gates.normative_summary: An original is renamed or moved and the companion restarts. It resolves where supported, or offers Locate. There is no stale-path fallback.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later, signed installed companion holding real security-scoped bookmarks across a restart.

evidence.covers: A stale root access becomes repairable and is repaired in place rather than falling back to a path.
An unresolvable root refuses reads until repaired, which is the no-stale-path-fallback rule.

gates.missing_condition: Every test substitutes a stub bookmark codec that encodes the path as Data(url.path.utf8). SystemSecurityScopedBookmarkCodec is never referenced by any test, so bookmark-based resolution of a renamed or moved original, which is the whole mechanism this gate tests, has never been exercised.
gates.limitations: The repair and refusal state machine is covered. Its input, a real resolved bookmark, is simulated by a path string, which resolves across a rename in exactly the way a real bookmark would not.

gates.normative_summary: An editor performs an atomic safe save. The result is a correct authorised replacement capture or an explicit recovery, with no permanent-inode assumption.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later, signed installed companion watching a file a real editor rewrites by rename.

evidence.covers: Changed bytes publish a new intent, which is the replacement-capture half for an ordinary rewrite.
The repair route a replaced file would take.

gates.missing_condition: No test performs a safe save, and the bookmark codec is stubbed everywhere, so the gate's distinguishing question, whether continuity survives an inode change, cannot be asked. A real editor and a real security-scoped bookmark on a signed installed build are required.
gates.limitations: Only the ordinary changed-bytes path is covered, which is the case a safe save is specifically not.

gates.normative_summary: A file changes during reading. The result is consistent captured bytes or a bounded failure, and never metadata from one version paired with another version's payload.
gates.applicability: Every qualified source on every OS the Core runtime supports, plus the macOS companion preparation path.

evidence.covers: A file modified mid-read is refused rather than captured inconsistently.
A path rebound mid-read is refused.
Growth past the limit during the read is a bounded failure.
The companion freezes the bytes it publishes.

gates.missing_condition: The Python refusals belong to the engineering source-capture read path, not to the macOS document-intake preparation path the gate is about. No test on the companion side changes a file while CapturePreparationCoordinator is reading it, so the metadata-payload pairing invariant is unproven where it matters.
gates.limitations: Mid-read refusal is demonstrated on a different read path in a different language. Reusing it as evidence here would be exactly the similarly-named-test substitution this ledger is meant to prevent, so it is listed as partial only.

gates.normative_summary: An original is deleted, replaced by an unrelated file, or moved across volumes. Availability is truthful, and relink is explicit when continuity is ambiguous.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later, signed installed companion holding real grants across local and removable volumes.

evidence.covers: Relink advances the generation, so a relinked original cannot be read under the old binding.
An inaccessible original refuses reads rather than reporting availability.
On the Core side relink advances the generation and keeps the old one historical.

gates.missing_condition: Cross-volume moves need a second real volume, and the same-name-unrelated-file case needs a real bookmark to disagree with a path. Both are unavailable while the bookmark codec is stubbed in every test and CI mounts no extra volume.
gates.limitations: Relink mechanics are covered on both sides. The three triggering situations the gate names are not reproduced; only their consequences are.

gates.normative_summary: An iCloud placeholder or an offline removable drive. The UI stays responsive and the download or unavailable state is accurate. There is no empty success.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later, signed installed companion against each qualified cloud provider and a removable volume, on the minimum supported hardware section 17.4 names.

evidence.covers: An unavailable provider reports that nothing was covered, which is the no-empty-success rule.
The production residency probe qualifies itself before claiming a residency answer.

gates.missing_condition: Two separate things are absent. There is no iCloud, File Provider, network-volume or removable-volume fixture anywhere in the repository and CI mounts none, so no qualified provider's real placeholder behaviour has been observed. Separately, the responsive-UI half is a measurement: section 17.4 sets a warm popover under 200 ms p95 and a local item under 64 KiB publishing within 500 ms p95 on minimum hardware, and no p95 measurement of any UI or publication path exists in this repository.
gates.limitations: The no-empty-success invariant is proven against an injected unavailable provider, which is the truthfulness half. Responsiveness is not measured anywhere, for any provider, and no CPU, memory, wakeup or disk peak is recorded, so the operational qualification section 17.4 requires has no results at all.

gates.normative_summary: Locate is used during preparation. The old binding generation cannot publish the new file under a stale association.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion with a preparation in flight while the grant generation advances.

evidence.covers: A generation change after the reads rejects the whole batch rather than publishing under the old association.
A stale root generation can neither read nor publish.
Relink is what advances the generation the rejection keys on.

gates.missing_condition: The generation fence is covered, but it is never driven by an actual Locate action. No test invokes Locate, because the chooser that performs it lives in the panel and management UI, neither of which has a test that reaches the preparation coordinator.
gates.limitations: The fence is the right mechanism and is well covered as a mechanism. The gate asks about the Locate path specifically, and that path is not connected to it in any test.

gates.normative_summary: Disconnect races a final multi-file publication. All generations and tokens are revalidated atomically with publication, and a revocation that wins prevents the entire stale batch from publishing.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion publishing a multi-item batch while a disconnect commits.

evidence.covers: A generation change rejects the whole batch, not the affected item alone.
Nothing can interleave between validation, the rename and completion, which is the atomicity the gate requires.
One shared publication gate across every owner, so the race has a single serialisation point.
A refused two-item batch exposes neither item.

gates.missing_condition: Every covered interleaving is a pause or a subscription change. No test commits an actual Disconnect against an in-flight multi-file publication, so the specific revocation-wins ordering the gate names is not exercised.
gates.limitations: Atomicity, whole-batch rejection and the single gate are all well covered. The revoking operation used is not the one the gate names.

gates.normative_summary: Disconnect after durable publication, including before the first admission. The queued or accepted snapshot can be admitted as historical and finish under current authority, and a tombstone prevents active-binding recreation and stale head promotion.
gates.applicability: The Core canonical admission boundary on every OS the runtime supports, for sources the companion has disconnected.

evidence.covers: Disconnect before any capture writes an owner-scoped tombstone, which is the before-first-admission case.
A removed source still admits captures, but only as history, and keeps its existing heads.
A removed capture is never promoted to head, which is the no-stale-head-promotion requirement.
The tombstone is owner scoped, so it prevents recreation of this binding without affecting another owner's.

gates.limitations: Core side only, against the real SQLite store and ServiceRunner in a single process. No companion participates, so the queued snapshot is constructed by calling the service rather than arriving from a durable native queue, and the tombstone is never raced against a concurrent admission from another process.

gates.normative_summary: A disconnect acknowledgement is lost. Local revocation persists and same-key canonical reconciliation resumes.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion and the Core admission boundary, across a lost acknowledgement.

evidence.covers: Local revocation covers every route for that document and no other.
The canonical side of the disconnect is idempotent under the same owner key.

gates.missing_condition: No test loses a disconnect acknowledgement. Lost-acknowledgement recovery is covered for handoff adoption and for capture publication, but not for revocation, so nothing shows the local revocation surviving and the reconciliation resuming on the same key.
gates.limitations: Both halves exist as separate capabilities on separate sides. The gate is about their interaction across a dropped message, and no test spans the two.

gates.normative_summary: Two refreshes finish in reverse order. The newer successful head remains, and the older capture can remain historical.
gates.applicability: The Core canonical capture and head-ordering boundary on every OS the runtime supports.

evidence.covers: A revision completing after a newer one is superseded and the newer head stands, which is exactly the reverse-order case.
The older capture is kept as history rather than discarded.
The late arrival is told it is no longer the head instead of silently winning.

gates.limitations: Core side only, in one process against the real SQLite store. The two refreshes are sequenced deterministically by the test rather than genuinely raced, so the ordering invariant is proven over the commit sequence and not over concurrent writers.

gates.normative_summary: A refresh fails after a previous success. The prior capture remains available, and the failure is shown separately.
gates.applicability: The Core canonical capture boundary and the companion state projection.

evidence.covers: A refresh that cannot read its source keeps the previous head available.
A failed head advance rolls back rather than leaving a half-applied state.

gates.missing_condition: The prior head's survival is covered, but no test asserts the failed refresh is retrievable as its own distinct outcome. Nothing shows the failure recorded separately from the surviving success, which is the second half of the required result.
gates.limitations: Core side only. The companion projection that would show the two states side by side has no test for this pairing.

gates.normative_summary: The same bytes, but the evidence has expired or been revoked. There is no false Already up to date, and the retention and authorisation policy is respected.
gates.applicability: The Core canonical retention boundary and the companion unchanged-digest path.

evidence.covers: An expired head does not fall back to an older capture.
Retention only moves forward, so a revoked capture cannot be revived.
The unchanged-digest short circuit exists on the companion side, which is the behaviour this gate requires be suppressed when evidence has expired.

gates.missing_condition: No test combines the two conditions. The unchanged-digest short circuit is covered only with valid evidence, and expiry is covered only on the Core side, so nothing shows the companion declining to report up to date when the evidence behind those bytes has expired or been revoked.
gates.limitations: Each condition is covered alone, which is the configuration in which the defect this gate guards against cannot appear.

gates.normative_summary: A text-bearing PDF. The binary source is retained, page provenance is correct, and the text is retrievable before Added.
gates.applicability: Every qualified PDF on every OS the Core runtime supports. The extractor is platform-agnostic Python over pypdfium2.

evidence.covers: Native page text is extracted with correct page provenance.
The binary source is admitted and retained without being inlined.
A pending capture becomes a searchable projection, which is retrieval before the canonical Added state.

gates.missing_condition: The PDF fixture is synthesised in-test with no recorded fixture digest, and section 11.15 requires the exact engine, profile, resource and fixture hashes be recorded with the result. No such record exists for any DOC or AT document gate.
gates.limitations: All three required properties have a direct test against the production extractor. What is absent is the qualification record, not the behaviour, and the retrievable-before-Added case is proven for a text capture rather than specifically for the PDF.

gates.normative_summary: A mixed ten-page PDF fixture. Full Text and local OCR expose all qualified text exactly once, and a two-page OCR failure or an explicit Text-only profile shows exact missing coverage.
gates.applicability: Every qualified PDF on hosts where the pinned OCR engine and its language models are installed.

evidence.covers: A mixed page retains both its native region and its OCR-only region.
A per-unit failure keeps exact counts and a partial outcome rather than a whole-document failure.
A Text-only profile names the exact pages it did not examine.
The one real-engine integration case, which deduplicates the sample PDF exactly once.

gates.missing_condition: There is no ten-page mixed fixture. The real-engine case is a single small sample PDF and is skipped unless the host has tesseract and English models, which neither CI workflow nor scripts/preflight installs, so on CI it does not run at all. No fixture hash is recorded for any PDF.
gates.limitations: The merge, dedup, partial-outcome and missing-coverage contracts are covered deterministically with an injected engine. The gate's specific fixture, its page count and its exactly-once property at that scale are not.

gates.normative_summary: Image-only, encrypted, corrupt and limit-exceeding PDFs. Image-only enters qualified OCR, encrypted, invalid and over-limit cases have bounded truthful outcomes, and job creation is not success.
gates.applicability: Every qualified PDF on every OS the Core runtime supports.

evidence.covers: Corrupt and encrypted PDFs are bounded refusals.
An over-limit source is refused before any decoding.
A missing model is a needs-language outcome, never a success.
A corrupt PDF is preserved and settled with no searchable projection, so creating the job was not success.

gates.missing_condition: The image-only-enters-qualified-OCR half needs the pinned engine and an installed language model. That path is covered only with an injected engine, and the real-engine case is skipped on CI because tesseract is not installed, so no run demonstrates an image-only PDF actually entering qualified recognition.
gates.limitations: Three of the four named situations are covered directly against the production extractor. The fourth is covered structurally but never with a real recognition pass.

gates.normative_summary: One item fails before local publication, and separately a partial Core processing case. A preparation failure publishes none and retains the draft. After publication, successful evidence is preserved with exact per-item outcomes.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion multi-item submission, and the Core processing boundary for a partially successful document.

evidence.covers: A preparation failure publishes nothing at all.
A refused multi-item batch exposes neither item, which is the publishes-none requirement.
A partial Core processing case keeps exact per-unit counts and a partial outcome.
One unreadable member needs attention while its siblings still publish, with per-child outcomes.
A preparation failure publishes none of the batch, connects no grant and leaves the reviewed draft, its note and its mode intact for the person to correct.

gates.limitations: Publishes-none, draft retention and per-item outcomes are each asserted against the production submission path. The preparation failure is injected by deleting one reviewed file after review, so one failure kind stands for all of them; retention is checked over the draft's display names rather than its URLs; and the partial Core case is a Core-side raster test, not a companion talking to a real service.

gates.normative_summary: A Core-only installation. Add, retrieve, manage the original and recover all work without Platform or an AI account setup.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later, signed installed companion with Platform absent and no AI account configured.

evidence.covers: The companion binds to the runtime's local principal, so no account configuration is required to deliver.
The installed companion's target derivation matches the CLI's, so a Core-only install addresses the same target.

gates.missing_condition: A clean Core-only installation can only be exercised against an installed signed build and a real installed Core service. No test installs anything, and the delivery client is a fake in every companion test.
gates.limitations: Target derivation agreement is proven as a value comparison. Nothing performs an Add, a retrieve, a manage-original or a recovery against a real service.

gates.normative_summary: Core and Platform coexistence. One companion, shared authoritative records, and no duplicated watcher or queue.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later with Platform absent, installed, running and closed.

evidence.covers: A second launch forwards a fixed refresh intent and exits, which is the one-companion rule.

gates.missing_condition: Platform is not present in this repository in any form, so coexistence cannot be exercised here at all. The design's requirement of one setting value and one watcher registry across both products has no second participant to test against.
gates.limitations: Only the single-instance lock is covered, and only within one process tree using an owner-only lock file and a Unix socket in a temporary directory.

gates.normative_summary: A compatible signed update, and a downgrade. Access persists where qualified, and pending schemas are preserved or clearly blocked.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later across a signed update and a rollback of the companion and its extensions.

evidence.covers: A newer schema is clearly blocked and its bytes are left intact, which is the downgrade-preservation half.
A newer Share manifest is preserved byte for byte so a newer build can still adopt it.
The scheduling document from a newer build is refused and left exactly as it was.
A legacy grant layout migrates forward rather than being dropped, which is the access-persists half.

gates.missing_condition: No signed build exists to update or roll back, and the access-persistence half depends on real security-scoped bookmarks surviving a reinstall, which cannot be shown while every test stubs the bookmark codec.
gates.limitations: Forward-compatibility and schema preservation are covered thoroughly at the store level. The update and downgrade events themselves are simulated by writing a document with a different version number.

gates.normative_summary: Clear receipts, disconnect and uninstall. Each has a distinct effect, and original documents remain unchanged.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later, signed installed companion, all three operations.

evidence.covers: Disconnect revokes every route for one document and affects no other.
Original bytes and filesystem attributes are unchanged by a capture run.

gates.missing_condition: Uninstall is owned by an installer that does not exist, and clearing receipts is a management-UI action with no test. Only disconnect has coverage, so the distinctness of the three effects is not demonstrated.
gates.limitations: The originals-unchanged invariant is covered for a folder run against a temporary directory. The three operations the gate contrasts are not exercised together anywhere.

gates.normative_summary: Keyboard and VoiceOver. Every capture and recovery action is usable without drag, and focus and announcements are accurate.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later, installed companion, with VoiceOver enabled and drag unavailable.

evidence.covers: Two review-first App Intents exist, which is one non-drag route into capture.
The picker route exists as a non-drag alternative to the status-item drop.

gates.missing_condition: There is no accessibility test anywhere in the repository and no VoiceOver qualification record. Accessibility labels are set in only five source files, and no test reads one. Focus order and announcements require a human or an automated UI session on a real build, neither of which exists.
gates.limitations: The existence of non-drag routes is evidence that drag-free paths are designed, not that they are reachable, focusable or announced correctly. Nothing about VoiceOver has been exercised.

gates.normative_summary: Appearance, text scaling, and long or Unicode names. No clipping, no colour-only state and no unreadable controls.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later installed companion in light and dark appearance, at every supported text size.
gates.missing_condition: No screenshot, snapshot or image-diff test exists, and there is no text-scaling or Dynamic Type coverage of any kind. Dark mode and appearance appear only in source and README prose. Visual qualification requires a rendered build and a reviewer.
gates.limitations: There is no evidence of any kind for this gate. The CoreSettingsPreview and CoreCaptureHarness executables are manual launchers and produce no recorded result.

gates.normative_summary: Multiple displays, menu edges, a hidden menu bar and fullscreen. Capture and dismissal stay usable, and no control becomes unreachable.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later installed companion across multi-display, hidden-menu-bar and fullscreen configurations.

evidence.covers: The hover affordance is clamped to the visible screen frame, which is the near-edge arithmetic this gate depends on.

gates.missing_condition: The clamp is tested against injected screen rectangles. No test attaches a second display, hides the menu bar, enters fullscreen or removes a display, and NSScreen is never driven by a real configuration anywhere.
gates.limitations: One geometric helper is covered with synthetic rectangles. The gate's configurations are not reproducible without a real window server session and more than one display.

gates.normative_summary: A native-to-Core arbitrary path injection attempt. The access owner or client rejects authority injection, and reads remain bound to the selected originals.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion access owner and every route that resolves a source for reading.

evidence.covers: Member resolution refuses a symlink escape out of the approved root.
Malformed routes and peer requirements fail closed rather than resolving.
Event translation keeps only root-relative components inside registered roots, so no absolute path crosses the boundary.
A member moved outside its root cannot be read through the root authority.

gates.missing_condition: Every test substitutes a stub bookmark codec encoding the path as Data(url.path.utf8), so no test shows a real security-scoped resolution refusing an injected path. Containment is proven over path components, which is one of the two mechanisms the gate relies on; the grant itself is not.
gates.limitations: Component-bounded containment and fail-closed route parsing are strong and directly tested. They are enforced in-process with no sandbox, and the grant that is meant to make them unforgeable is simulated.

gates.normative_summary: Source and derived claims retrieval. Source evidence and any derived knowledge retain correct attribution, and nothing is auto-approved.
gates.applicability: The Core governed-knowledge boundary on every OS the runtime supports, for evidence captured from any intake route.

evidence.covers: A derived proposal cannot approve itself without an admission reference.
A verified role and an unverified claim stay distinct, which is the attribution requirement.
A derived case stays proposed until an owner reviews it, so there is no auto-approval.

gates.missing_condition: The governed-knowledge tests operate on knowledge items that did not come from a document capture. No test derives a claim from a captured document's extracted evidence and then checks the attribution chain back to that source, which is the linkage this gate is about.
gates.limitations: No-auto-approval is well covered in the governance layer. Its connection to document intake attribution is not covered at all, so the two halves of the gate are proven over different subjects.

gates.normative_summary: An earlier snapshot is admitted after a newer capture succeeds. A frozen base mismatch produces a historical-only disposition, and a larger arrival sequence does not replace the newer successful head.
gates.applicability: The Core canonical admission and head-ordering boundary on every OS the runtime supports.

evidence.covers: A frozen base mismatch yields a historical-only disposition and never the head.
A later arrival does not displace the newer successful head, so arrival order is not the ordering authority.
History remains navigable rather than collapsing once a capture is historical.

gates.limitations: Core side only, single process, against the real SQLite store. The late admission is applied by the test in a chosen order rather than arriving concurrently, so the invariant is proven over commit sequence and not under genuine contention. No companion queue supplies the snapshot.

gates.normative_summary: A descriptor expires with a known-no-effect outcome, versus an ambiguous admission. Only a conclusive no-effect permits a new child generation or key; old attempts are retained and the parent is deduplicated. Unknown outcomes reconcile their original request.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion durable intent queue and the Core staged-transfer boundary.

evidence.covers: Only exact known-no-effect evidence permits a retry under a new key; anything else must reconcile the original.
An interrupted stage becomes an explicit unknown rather than being retried blindly.
Old attempts are retained across a restart rather than discarded.
On the Core side a staged transfer key cannot be rebound to different bytes, which deduplicates the parent.

gates.limitations: The companion half runs in an unsigned swift test process on the macos-latest runner with OS and Xcode versions unrecorded, and expiry is injected rather than observed from a real descriptor timing out. The Core half is a separate single-process test, so the two keyspaces are proven compatible by construction rather than by one end-to-end run.

gates.normative_summary: An external access-owner call against a candidate or a provisional binding. Unsubmitted candidates cannot read, provisional Refresh, Open and Reveal are denied, only the scoped intent can prepare, and published recovery never rereads the original.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion access owner, candidate store and management surface.

evidence.covers: An adopted but unsubmitted candidate is neither enumerated nor captured.
Root authority stays provisional until its durable owner exists.
Published recovery continues without rereading bytes it already published.
Recovery restores candidates without copying the source again.

gates.missing_condition: No test covers Refresh, Open or Reveal against a provisional binding. Those three actions live in FilesAndFoldersModel and FolderManagementWindowController, and neither has a case that attempts one before the binding is durable.
gates.limitations: Three of the four named conditions are covered directly. The denial of the three user actions, which is the clause naming specific operations, has no assertion anywhere.

gates.normative_summary: Evidence is retrievable while the requested linkage is pending. Progress or attention persists until the canonical association is confirmed, with no provisional active-link row and no premature linked-capture success.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion management surface and the Core association boundary.

evidence.covers: The Link an original chooser request opens review exactly once rather than reporting a link it does not have.
A snapshot submission does not invent an original binding, which is the no-provisional-row rule at submission.

gates.missing_condition: No test holds a pending linkage request and then asserts the projected row stays in progress or attention until the canonical association is confirmed. FilesAndFoldersModel has no pending-linkage case, so the persistence requirement is unproven.
gates.limitations: The two references show a link is never fabricated at submission time. They say nothing about the state shown while a real linkage request is outstanding.

gates.normative_summary: Direct icon drop. One or many original files, supported content, promises, and mixed files and folders each open the correct review exactly once. No original bytes or attributes are mutated by capture.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later, signed installed companion with a live status item receiving real drag sessions.

evidence.covers: One drag session reaches review exactly once.
Promised files are reported once, in the order the source promised them.
A mixed file and folder drop is classified in the order given.
Original bytes and attributes are unchanged by a capture run.

gates.missing_condition: Section 20.1 requires evidence in an installed signed build. The packaging manifest records the candidate as unsigned and not release eligible, no drag session is ever performed, and StatusItemDropView has no test.
gates.limitations: The drag policy is proven as a pure function over declared pasteboard types and counts. Nothing exercises NSDraggingDestination, the status button's child view, or a real promise provider.

gates.normative_summary: Native status behaviour. Left and right click, keyboard activation, VoiceOver, Command-drag reorder and removal, opening the menu, hover exit and subsequent clicks all retain correct behaviour with the drop adapter installed.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later installed companion status item with the transparent drop child attached.

evidence.covers: The hover affordance delay, which is the timing the hover-exit behaviour depends on.

gates.missing_condition: Every condition this gate lists is an input event delivered by the window server to an installed status item. No click, keypress, Command-drag or VoiceOver interaction is performed anywhere in the repository, and there is no accessibility test of any kind.
gates.limitations: Only one timing constant is covered. The gate's whole point, that the adapter does not break the status item's native behaviour, is untested in every respect.

gates.normative_summary: Display and accessibility. A hidden menu bar, fullscreen, multiple displays, display removal, a near-edge icon, Dark Mode, Reduce Motion and text scaling all leave no unreachable or orphan UI.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later installed companion across every supported display and appearance configuration.

evidence.covers: The near-edge clamp keeps the affordance inside the visible screen frame.

gates.missing_condition: There is no visual, appearance, Reduce Motion, text-scaling or multi-display test anywhere, and no accessibility qualification record. The clamp is the only piece with coverage, and it is exercised against injected rectangles rather than real screens.
gates.limitations: One geometric helper, with synthetic input. Nothing shows what happens when a display is removed while the affordance is on it, which is the orphan-UI case the gate names.

gates.normative_summary: Drag operation semantics. Copy-permitted sources work and move-only sources are rejected. Modifier keys never convert ingestion into source mutation.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later installed companion status item receiving real drag sessions with and without modifier keys.

evidence.covers: The drop route's admission decision, which is where the returned operation is chosen.
Capture does not mutate the source, which is the consequence a modifier key must not be able to change.

gates.missing_condition: No test asserts the returned NSDragOperation is copy, and no test supplies a move-only source or a modifier key. The README states the view returns copy only; nothing checks it, and a real drag session is required to observe what the source then does.
gates.limitations: The policy that decides admission is covered. The operation it reports back to the drag source, which is the entire subject of this gate, is not asserted anywhere.

gates.normative_summary: File promises. Export failure, cancellation, capacity exhaustion and producer termination create truthful rows and no queued acknowledgement. Completed owned bytes survive provider expiry.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later installed companion receiving real NSFilePromiseReceiver deliveries.

evidence.covers: A failed promise settles and is not reported as delivered.
Producer termination is bounded by the delivery timeout and late callbacks are ignored.
A provider that overruns its declared size or misnames its file settles nothing.
Completed owned bytes survive the source going away.

gates.missing_condition: Section 20.1 requires an installed signed build. The promise state machine is driven by a test harness standing in for NSFilePromiseReceiver, so no real producer ever exports, cancels or dies, and no queued acknowledgement is observed being withheld by the real queue.
gates.limitations: The failure, timeout and overrun paths are covered well as pure state transitions on a temporary directory. Capacity exhaustion is covered on the quota side rather than from a promise, and the truthful-rows half is a projection no test reads.

gates.normative_summary: Native Quick Action preservation. An installed viewer-role action appears for the intended single and multiple files and directories. Success, handoff, cancel, error and host termination all leave original Finder URLs, bytes and attributes unchanged.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later, signed installed Finder Action extension macOS has registered.

evidence.covers: Writes the NSExtension block and activation rule for the com.apple.ui-services Action extension into the generated plist.
The packaged app embeds real Finder Action and Share appex bundles under Contents/PlugIns.
The extension completes only once every offered slot is adopted.
A mixed file and directory selection keeps its order and acknowledges only after every adoption.

gates.missing_condition: FinderActionViewController is not a Swift Package target, has no tests, and is not even typechecked by CI. Whether the action appears in Finder for the intended selections can only be observed on a signed installed build macOS has registered, and no signed build exists.
gates.limitations: The companion side of the handoff is covered well. The extension that returns the NSExtensionItem objects unmodified, which is the preservation claim, has no automated coverage at all.

gates.normative_summary: Representation identity. Actual Finder originals, local-copy providers, exports and preview-text alternatives each take their specified routes. No temporary path becomes a linked original.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later installed companion across the Finder, Share, drop and Shortcuts routes.

evidence.covers: Alternative representations of one logical item collapse to one slot in a fixed preference order.
The fixed representation preference order, so a preview-text alternative cannot displace the real payload.
A snapshot never acquires an original binding, so a temporary path cannot become a linked original.
Each surface keeps its own provenance through review, which is the routes-stay-distinct requirement.

gates.missing_condition: The representations the gate distinguishes are supplied by real NSItemProvider instances from real host applications. Every test constructs them directly, so nothing shows a genuine local-copy provider or export being classified, and an installed signed build is required to receive one.
gates.limitations: The classification rules and the no-temporary-original invariant are covered directly and are strong. Their inputs are synthetic, so the mapping from a real provider to a route is untested.

gates.normative_summary: Access handoff. A real implicit transfer is resolved while valid, and only companion-created persistent access survives restart. Copied explicit extension bookmarks, expired tokens and forged peer claims all fail safely.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later, signed installed companion and extensions sharing an App Group, with real security-scoped bookmarks and real code-signing identities.

evidence.covers: Expired, mismatched and traversal offers are rejected.
The peer requirement rejects invalid inputs.
A companion-created grant persists owner-only and balances its access, which is the survives-restart half.
The peer socket reports the kernel's own peer uid and pid rather than a claimed identity.

gates.missing_condition: Two mechanisms this gate rests on are never exercised. Every test substitutes a stub bookmark codec encoding the path as Data(url.path.utf8), so SystemSecurityScopedBookmarkCodec and real implicit transfer resolution are untested. Peer verification is covered only on its input-validation path: designatedRequirement, SecCodeCheckValidity against a signed peer, and NativeHandoffPeerServer rejection have no test, and a forged peer claim cannot be constructed without signed identities.
gates.limitations: The mailbox nonce, expiry and traversal rules are well covered, and the socket does report real kernel peer identity, but for an unsigned test process. The copied-explicit-bookmark case cannot even be represented while the codec is a path string.

gates.normative_summary: Cold companion. Actual Action and Share targets can use the chosen supported activation path where advertised, and launch failure or manual continuation is truthful. No second companion or Core authority appears.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later, signed installed extensions activating a companion that is not running.

evidence.covers: A request made while the companion was closed is adopted at startup, which is the manual-continuation path.
A second launch forwards one fixed intent and exits, so no second companion appears.

gates.missing_condition: Activation of a non-running companion by an extension requires macOS to have registered that extension from a signed installed build. No test launches a process from an extension, and the truthfulness of the launch-failure wording is not asserted anywhere.
gates.limitations: Durable continuation while closed and the single-instance rule are both covered. The activation attempt itself, which is what the gate is about, is not performed.

gates.normative_summary: Lost handoff acknowledgement. The same request and slot-to-candidate mapping recovers without duplicate drafts, grants or captures. An existing draft permits prompt waiting-queue adoption, and no Core destination is required before Add. Destination changes, transfer expiry, candidate lifetime and cancel or publication ownership follow their separate boundaries.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion and extensions sharing the App Group handoff mailbox.

evidence.covers: A lost acknowledgement reconciles against the same adoption rather than creating a second.
The Share route recovers without copying the bytes again.
An exact replay maps to the same refs and adopts once, which is the slot-to-candidate mapping requirement.
Failure injected at every boundary converges on the same adoption.
Candidate lifetime is independent of the transfer window, which is one of the separate boundaries.

gates.missing_condition: Section 20.1 requires an installed signed build. The recovery logic is exercised exhaustively, but both participants are the same test process against a temporary directory, with no App Group, no extension and no real transfer expiry clock.
gates.limitations: This is the best-covered native gate in the repository and the convergence properties are genuinely strong. What is untested is that a real extension and a real companion, in two processes under macOS extension lifetime rules, reach the same convergence.

gates.normative_summary: Folder picker and drop. Add current files and Watch folder mode, and recursion and exclusions, are explicit. Package and alias escape and out-of-root locators are denied. Over-limit scope produces no silent partial enrolment.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later installed companion folder picker and folder drop routes.

evidence.covers: An over-limit scope is refused and enrols nothing, so there is no silent partial enrolment.
Packages and bundles are neither descended into nor accepted.
Symlinks and Finder aliases are never followed, which is the escape denial.
Recursion off never lists a subfolder, so recursion is explicit rather than advisory.
The folder picker policy is fixed to one directory and no file.

gates.missing_condition: Section 20.1 requires an installed signed build. No NSOpenPanel is presented and no folder drop is performed, so the two routes the gate names are never driven; only the scope policy behind them is exercised.
gates.limitations: Scope, recursion, exclusion and escape denial are covered thoroughly against real temporary directory trees. Mode selection is covered as a policy value, and the two entry routes are not exercised at all.

gates.normative_summary: Frozen import membership. A retained RootAccessGroup allows authorised manual actions only on enrolled members, and cannot discover or capture newly appearing siblings without a new explicit scope.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later, signed installed companion retaining a root grant across restarts.

evidence.covers: A sibling created later is refused after a restart, which is the no-discovery requirement.
The completed plan narrows to frozen members only while keeping manual member reads.
Members share one persisted root grant until the last owner releases it.

gates.missing_condition: The retained authority is a security-scoped bookmark, and every test substitutes a stub codec encoding the path as Data(url.path.utf8). A path string resolves across restarts unconditionally, so retention of the real grant, which is what this gate qualifies, has never been exercised.
gates.limitations: The frozen-membership logic is well covered and is genuinely independent of the codec. The authority that is supposed to make it enforceable rather than advisory is simulated.

gates.normative_summary: Repeated and external invocations. Hover callbacks, repeated Shortcut and Finder invocations, existing drafts and rapid mixed drops do not overwrite or silently merge unrelated intent.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later installed companion across the Shortcuts, Finder and drop routes under repeated invocation.

evidence.covers: Repeated Shortcut runs wait rather than merge.
One drag session is admitted once, so a repeated hover or drop cannot double-admit it.
Confirming one group never submits another, which is the no-silent-merge requirement.
A conflicting replay fails and changes nothing rather than overwriting the original intent.

gates.missing_condition: Section 20.1 requires an installed signed build. Hover callbacks and rapid mixed drops cannot be produced without a real drag source, and repeated Finder invocations need a registered Services entry or Action extension; neither exists.
gates.limitations: The no-merge and no-overwrite invariants are covered on the Shortcuts, group and replay paths. The hover and rapid-drop conditions the gate names specifically are not reproduced.

gates.normative_summary: Keyboard and Shortcuts. Every capture and recovery path is reachable without drag, typed IntentFile expiry is handled, foreground incompatibility is reported, and Shortcut completion never falsely means Added to Core.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later installed companion, every capture and recovery path, with drag unavailable.

evidence.covers: The intent owns a copy of every supplied representation before perform returns, which is how IntentFile expiry is handled.
Exactly two review-first intents are offered, so no Shortcut can report an Add.
The opening intent only opens the panel and reads nothing.
An empty or oversize typed selection is refused.

gates.missing_condition: The reachable-without-drag claim spans every capture and recovery path, and there is no accessibility or keyboard test anywhere to establish it. Foreground incompatibility reporting is not asserted, and the Shortcut completion wording is never read by a test. A registered App Intents provider on an installed build is required.
gates.limitations: The two intents' ownership, bounds and review-first behaviour are covered directly. Coverage of the gate's actual subject, keyboard reachability of every path, is zero.

gates.normative_summary: Fresh install and enablement. Actual Services, Quick Actions and Share discovery, the disabled-extension state, system keyboard settings and a Core-only installation all work without Developer Mode or a running Xcode project.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later clean host, signed installed companion, no development tooling present.

evidence.covers: The packaged bundle identity is stable and the manifest records the candidate as unsigned and not release eligible.
The packaging refuses to emit a bundle with only one of the two extensions, so an enablement test could not be run against a half-built app.

gates.missing_condition: This gate is the signed-install qualification itself. No codesign, spctl, notarytool or stapler invocation exists in the repository, the packaging manifest declares the candidate qualification_only and unsigned, and nothing registers extensions with pluginkit or reads a disabled-extension state.
gates.limitations: Only the deterministic bundle layout is covered. The README states explicitly that ad-hoc signing is not evidence that macOS has registered App Group-backed extensions, and nothing beyond ad-hoc signing has been attempted.

gates.normative_summary: Coherent update. App, extension and helper version skew, an old running extension, a compatible update, a rollback and a reinstallation all preserve durable work or block explicitly. Source grants are not silently lost or reactivated.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later across signed updates and rollbacks of the companion and both extensions.

evidence.covers: A newer schema from a future build is preserved byte for byte rather than rewritten.
An unsupported newer batch schema is preserved rather than discarded, which is the skew case.
A legacy folder ledger gets a default root generation frozen across updates, so grants are not silently reactivated.
Contradictory legacy grant records fail closed rather than picking one.

gates.missing_condition: No signed build exists to update, and no installer owns the update. An old running extension against a new companion requires two signed bundles and macOS extension lifetime behaviour; the grant-preservation half additionally requires real bookmarks, which are stubbed in every test.
