gates.limitations: The resident-only rule and the probe's self-qualification are covered against an injected provider. The gate's specific transition, first readable content becoming a baseline rather than a capture, is not asserted anywhere.

gates.normative_summary: An edit during a baseline or a scan. The persisted event obligation is reconciled, and baseline semantics and coverage are reported honestly.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion with an observation ledger and a reconciliation pass in flight.

evidence.covers: Events arriving during the scan survive the acknowledgement of that scan.
An obligation merged mid-pass survives the acknowledgement.
A bounded scan is reported as a pass that did not finish, which is honest coverage.
A partly failed subtree leaves the scan incomplete rather than reporting success.
A partial scan neither acknowledges its obligation nor damages the prior inventory.

gates.limitations: Unsigned swift test process on the macos-latest runner, OS and Xcode versions unrecorded. Events are injected rather than delivered by FSEvents, and the clock is injected, so the mid-pass edit is a method call placed between two steps rather than a real concurrent write. Section 21.12's signed installed access and real retrieval are not provided.

gates.normative_summary: A burst of saves. Signals coalesce before publication, each published snapshot remains immutable, and the latest dirty state is eventually checked.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion watching a file or folder under rapid repeated writes.

evidence.covers: The quiet period holds the check until signals stop, which is coalescing before publication.
A maximum wait publishes even under continuous signals, so coalescing cannot starve the check.
Signals after a published check become one dirty obligation, so the latest state is eventually checked.
Work behind a published claim waits for completion rather than racing it.
Each published snapshot is frozen at publication, which is the immutability requirement.

gates.limitations: Unsigned swift test process on the macos-latest runner, OS and Xcode versions unrecorded. The clock is injected and the burst is a sequence of method calls rather than real saves generating FSEvents, so the coalescing window is proven against simulated time. Section 21.12's signed installed access and real retrieval are not provided.

gates.normative_summary: A crash after a checkpoint. Every checkpointed relevant event has a durable obligation, and a restart does not lose the source check.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion observation ledger and scheduler across an unclean restart.

evidence.covers: Ingested obligations and the cursor survive a restart.
An unclean run owes full reconciliation for every affected subscription, so nothing checkpointed is lost.
A failed write advances neither the cursor nor the obligations, so a checkpoint is all or nothing.
Dirty work stays dirty and immediately due after a restart.
Armed work survives a restart.

gates.limitations: Unsigned swift test process on the macos-latest runner, OS and Xcode versions unrecorded. The crash is modelled by reopening the store without a clean close and by injected write failures; no process is killed and no power loss occurs, so the fsync and directory-durability barriers the design requires are not verified against a real interruption.

gates.normative_summary: A crash before the cursor update. Replay duplicates are harmless and do not create duplicate capture intentions.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion event ledger, intent queue and folder establishment across a replay.

evidence.covers: Event ids persist in order and the cursor never regresses, so a replay cannot rewind progress.
A revision is never reused after its obligation is cleared, so a duplicate cannot resurrect cleared work.
An exact replay reuses the published batch rather than creating a second intention.
Establishment replay is idempotent and a conflicting replay is refused.
A crash after run registration queues every child exactly once.

gates.limitations: Unsigned swift test process on the macos-latest runner, OS and Xcode versions unrecorded. The crash point is chosen by the test by stopping between store operations, so idempotency is proven over every modelled boundary but not against a real process kill. Events are injected rather than replayed by FSEvents.

gates.normative_summary: Dropped or coalesced events. Correct subtree or full-root reconciliation occurs, and pending callbacks alone never establish freshness.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion event bridge and scheduler on every watched root.

evidence.covers: Dropped, root-changed and must-scan flags become full reconciliation for the affected roots.
A scoped signal stays a subtree reconciliation and does not escalate to a full root scan.
A full reconciliation subsumes pending scopes while keeping every reason.
A history-done callback never clears obligations, so a pending callback cannot establish freshness.
Becoming due is not a claim of completed coverage.

gates.limitations: Unsigned swift test process on the macos-latest runner, OS and Xcode versions unrecorded. The dropped and coalesced flags are injected into the bridge rather than produced by a real FSEvents stream under load. The one unconditional real-FSEvents test covers a single recursive event, and the live-stream bridge case is skipped unless OMNIVIA_RUN_FSEVENTS_QUALIFICATION is set, which no workflow sets.

gates.normative_summary: The event UUID changes or is missing. The old history cursor is rejected, and a new observation epoch and a full scan begin.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion event bridge and observation ledger on every watched device.

evidence.covers: A changed, missing or future history opens a new epoch with full reconciliation.
A stream resumes from its cursor only when the UUID matches, which is the cursor rejection.
A changed stream identity opens a new epoch with full obligations and no comparable cursor.
Wrapped event ids can only continue through a new epoch.

gates.limitations: Unsigned swift test process on the macos-latest runner, OS and Xcode versions unrecorded. The UUIDs and event ids are injected, so the decision logic is fully covered but the real FSEvents history behaviour that would supply a changed UUID, such as a volume replacement, is never produced. Section 21.12 requires more than mocked filesystem events, and this is mocked events.

gates.normative_summary: Sleep, offline and remount. The current state catches up, and unavailable or partial coverage never becomes deletion.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later installed companion across real system sleep, network loss and volume remount.

evidence.covers: A wake trigger arms every active subscription.
A remount trigger arms every active subscription.
An unresolvable root is an unavailable provider rather than an absence.
Provider and residency gaps are never reported as complete coverage, which is what prevents a false deletion.

gates.missing_condition: Wake and remount are exercised as direct method calls on the driver. No test sleeps the machine, drops the network or mounts and unmounts a volume, and CI mounts no removable or network volume, so none of the three conditions the gate names is actually produced.
gates.limitations: The never-becomes-deletion invariant is covered well against injected unavailability, and the arming logic is covered for both triggers. What is missing is any real system event driving them.

gates.normative_summary: A network volume with no FSEvents history. Periodic checks work, and the UI does not imply immediate notifications.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later installed companion watching a network volume that supplies no event history.

evidence.covers: A subscription no stream observes is still armed durably, so periodic checks work without events.
The periodic intervals the fallback relies on are pinned.

gates.missing_condition: CI mounts no network volume, so no filesystem without FSEvents history has ever been watched. The second half of the gate is a UI claim, and no projection test asserts what the watch state says about notification immediacy for such a volume.
gates.limitations: The no-stream-still-armed case is covered, which is the right mechanism. It is covered by withholding a stream in a test rather than by a filesystem that cannot supply one, and the wording requirement has no coverage at all.

gates.normative_summary: Root rename or replacement. The same root can be followed when verified, and a new folder at its former path is not adopted silently.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later, signed installed companion holding a real root grant across a rename.

evidence.covers: A stale root becomes repairable and is repaired in place rather than rebound to whatever is at the path.
An unresolvable root refuses reads until repaired.
A stale root generation can neither read nor publish.

gates.missing_condition: Distinguishing the same renamed root from a different folder at its former path is precisely what a security-scoped bookmark resolves and a path string cannot. Every test substitutes a stub codec encoding the path as Data(url.path.utf8), under which a replacement at the same path is indistinguishable from the original, so this gate cannot be exercised here at all.
gates.limitations: The repair and refusal state machine is covered. Its discriminating input is simulated by the one value that makes the discrimination impossible.

gates.normative_summary: A child moves outside the root. Root-mediated reads stop and an unpublished candidate cannot publish, and independent route continuation is disclosed.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion watching a root whose member leaves it.

evidence.covers: A member moved outside the root cannot be read through the root authority.
An unpublished candidate under a stale generation cannot publish.
Containment is component bounded, so a move out of the root is detected structurally.
independentlyRoutedDocuments(routes:) selects only a connected direct-file route, excluding a disconnected one and a root membership.
A child that left the root is disclosed by name as still read through its own link, and a folder whose children have no link of their own says so instead.

gates.missing_condition: The disclosure is proven only over the model itself. independentlyRoutedDocuments(routes:) is driven with NativeAccessDescriptor values built in the test and the detail facts are driven with a hand-written document-id set, so nothing carries real NativeAccessStore routes through DocumentIntakeEnvironment.documentAccessRoutes() into the folder window. No companion flow mints a direct route sharing a folder member's linkedDocumentID either -- every submission path mints a fresh one -- so the pairing the disclosure describes is a capability of the store rather than a state the person can reach.
gates.limitations: The reads-stop and cannot-publish halves are covered directly against real temporary directories, and the route filter and both disclosure sentences are asserted against production code. The grant behind them is a stub bookmark codec.

gates.normative_summary: Symlink, alias, nested mount and path traversal. No bytes outside approved roots are opened, and a malicious manifest or relative locator is rejected.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion scope policy, access owner and event translation on every watched root.

evidence.covers: Symbolic links and Finder aliases are never followed.
A nested mount is not crossed.
Containment is component bounded rather than a string prefix, which is what defeats traversal.
Member resolution refuses a symlink escape out of the approved root.
Event translation keeps only root-relative components inside registered roots.
Malformed and out-of-scope relative locators are rejected by the ledger.
A Finder alias member route is refused rather than resolved.

gates.limitations: Unsigned swift test process on the macos-latest runner, OS and Xcode versions unrecorded. Containment is enforced in-process with no sandbox, so the refusals are the code's own rather than the kernel's, and the nested-mount case is exercised through a device-boundary check on temporary directories rather than against a real mounted volume. One unreadable-directory case is skipped when the test runs as root.

gates.normative_summary: Safe save versus unrelated replacement. Qualified native continuity preserves revision history, and an ambiguous replacement never merges histories by filename.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later, signed installed companion watching files a real editor rewrites by rename.

evidence.covers: Changed bytes publish a new intent against the existing source identity.
On the Core side a source identity cannot be rebound, which is what prevents histories merging.

gates.missing_condition: No test performs a safe save or an unrelated same-name replacement. The qualified native continuity the gate relies on is bookmark-based resolution across an inode change, and the bookmark codec is stubbed in every test, so continuity and ambiguity cannot be distinguished here.
gates.limitations: Only the ordinary changed-bytes path is covered on the companion side, which is the case a safe save specifically is not. The Core refusal is on the engineering source-capture path rather than the document-intake path.

gates.normative_summary: Confirmed deletion and reappearance. Evidence remains, and a new ambiguous same-name file does not impersonate the old original.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later, signed installed companion plus the Core retention boundary.

evidence.covers: A removed source keeps its heads, so the evidence remains.
A reappearance must relink, which advances the generation rather than reusing the old binding.

gates.missing_condition: Distinguishing a reappeared original from a new same-name file requires a real security-scoped bookmark, and every companion test stubs the codec to the path string, under which the two are identical. No test deletes and recreates a watched file either.
gates.limitations: The evidence-remains half is covered on the Core side. The impersonation half, which is the gate's actual subject, has no coverage on either side.

gates.normative_summary: Overlapping roots and a direct route. One verified source capture per workspace with multiple memberships, and no hash-based identity and no cross-workspace reuse.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion with overlapping watched roots and an independently watched member.

evidence.covers: Independent workspace and source identities do not coalesce, which is the no-cross-workspace-reuse rule.
A duplicate automatic source is rejected before a second capture, which is one capture per workspace.
Multiple memberships are held independently and release independently.
One grant serves multiple memberships until the last owner releases.

Two genuinely overlapping roots plus a direct route over the same file are configured, and no source identity, document id or scheduling key contains the file's content digest -- a byte-identical twin shares none of them, and rewriting the bytes changes none of them.

gates.missing_condition: No capture in the overlap reaches verified, and one capture with multiple memberships is not the structure this production path produces. Overlapping roots each mint their own member, source identity and queued intent, so the overlap test records three distinct operation keys for one file and admits none of them. What one verified source capture per workspace with multiple memberships should mean against that structure needs a design decision before a test could assert it.
gates.limitations: The no-hash-based-identity clause is now covered directly: every identity is a random-UUID identifier, the content digest occurs in none of them, and neither a byte-identical twin nor a rewrite changes that. Cross-workspace reuse is covered only as non-coalescing identities and a scheduling-key shape; a second workspace is never configured. Membership independence and duplicate rejection are covered. The grant is a stub bookmark codec.

gates.normative_summary: Stop watching. There is no new discovery and no automatic reads, and manual child routes remain functional.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion after a watch is stopped or paused, across the scheduler, driver and executor.

evidence.covers: A paused subscription schedules neither a metadata nor a content read.
No subscription outside the active state is ever read, so discovery stops at the executor too.
Pausing after work was already armed stops further arming.
The manual member route survives when the watch owner releases.
Manual member reads keep working once automatic scope narrows.

gates.limitations: Unsigned swift test process on the macos-latest runner, OS and Xcode versions unrecorded. The clock and the providers are injected, and the FSEvents stream is never actually torn down, so stopping is proven at the scheduling and reading layers rather than at the OS observation layer. Section 21.12's signed installed access and real retrieval are not provided.

gates.normative_summary: Source Disconnect versus folder Disconnect. The source action revokes all local routes and prevents rediscovery, and the folder action revokes only the route it owns.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion access owner and the Core tombstone boundary.

evidence.covers: The source action revokes every route for that document and no other.
A folder owner releases only its own route.
Releasing one owner never drops a grant another owner still holds.
The canonical tombstone is owner scoped.

A source Disconnect revokes that document's route and no other, and a later reconcileAll over a tree that still holds the file with changed bytes re-enrols nothing, queues nothing for it and refuses the read, while its sibling is still queued.

gates.limitations: Both revocation scopes and the rediscovery suppression are asserted against the production access store and folder coordinator over real temporary directories, including a second scan that queues nothing. Suppression is proven over the companion's own member ledger and its revoked-route skip, not against a grant the person re-authorises afterwards; the Core-side tombstone is owner scoped but does not itself stop a companion read; and the grant is a stub bookmark codec.

gates.normative_summary: Pause, configuration change or disconnect at the final rename. The shared publication lock yields a clear before-or-after outcome, and no stale generation publishes after revocation.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion publication gate, shared across every publication owner.

evidence.covers: A pause cannot interleave between validation, the rename and completion.
A pause cannot complete between consent validation and the commit, so the outcome is clearly before or after.
A configuration change during preparation rejects the whole batch.
A generation change after the reads prevents a stale generation from publishing.
The production environment shares one publication gate across every owner, which is the shared lock the gate names.
A state change inside the finalisation window commits neither half.

gates.limitations: Unsigned swift test process on the macos-latest runner, OS and Xcode versions unrecorded. The interleavings are injected at chosen points rather than produced by genuine concurrency, so the lock is proven to exclude every modelled interleaving rather than every possible one. Disconnect specifically is modelled as a generation change rather than performed as a disconnect.

gates.normative_summary: Core sees a tombstone before the first capture. A delayed immutable capture is historical-only and cannot recreate an active source route.
gates.applicability: The Core canonical admission boundary on every OS the runtime supports.

evidence.covers: A disconnect before the first capture writes the tombstone this gate starts from.
A capture arriving after the tombstone is admitted as history only.
Such a capture is never promoted, so it cannot recreate an active route.

gates.limitations: Core side only, in a single process against the real SQLite store and ServiceRunner. The delayed capture is applied by the test in the chosen order rather than arriving from a durable native queue after a real delay, so the invariant is proven over commit sequence rather than under genuine timing. No companion participates.

gates.normative_summary: A principal or target change. An existing pending intent is not redirected, and automatic reads pause under a changed identity.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion with pending automatic work when the signed-in identity changes.

evidence.covers: A pending intent under a mismatched caller context is not delivered, so it is not redirected.
The frozen caller binding must match at publication.
A subscription in any non-active state is left unscheduled, which is the mechanism a pause would use.

gates.missing_condition: No test changes the principal or the target profile and then asserts automatic reads pause. The refusals prove a pending intent is not redirected, but nothing moves a subscription into a paused state in response to an identity change, so the second half of the required result has no coverage.
gates.limitations: Caller and workspace identity are opaque values supplied by each test, with no authentication boundary involved. The pause mechanism exists and is covered, but never driven by an identity change.

gates.normative_summary: Offline with and without approved eligibility. Work queues only under an explicit valid owning policy, and no independent credential lease is taken.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion with no network, under each eligibility policy state.

evidence.covers: The companion binds to the runtime's local principal rather than holding a credential of its own.
An intent without its consent and lineage is rejected before it can be queued.

gates.missing_condition: No test takes the companion offline, and the eligibility policy the gate turns on is owned by the installed Core service, which no companion test talks to. Delivery is a fake in every case, so queuing-under-policy has never been exercised against a real authority.
gates.limitations: The no-independent-credential property is structural and is supported by the local-principal binding, but it is asserted as a value rather than observed under an offline condition. Neither eligibility state is produced.

gates.normative_summary: Cloud downloads disabled. Each qualified provider defers nonresident content, and uncertain availability cannot trigger an unapproved automatic download.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later installed companion against each qualified cloud provider with downloads disabled.

evidence.covers: A content pass digests resident members only, so nonresident content is deferred.
The residency probe qualifies itself before claiming, so an uncertain answer is not treated as resident.
A residency gap is never reported as complete coverage.

gates.missing_condition: There is no iCloud or File Provider fixture and CI mounts none, so no qualified provider has been exercised and the per-provider behaviour the gate requires cannot be enumerated. Residency is a fake in every test.
gates.limitations: The defer-and-never-force rule is covered against an injected provider and is the right invariant. The gate asks for it per qualified provider, which needs real provider mounts.

gates.normative_summary: A byte or copy quota is reached. Compact obligations remain, and no pending snapshot is silently evicted and no scan falsely completed.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion under native-owned quota pressure.

evidence.covers: At the bound a new request is refused rather than an existing one evicted.
The quota counts published and candidate bytes together, so pressure is accounted honestly.
Too many scopes collapse to one full reconciliation, which is the compact-obligation mechanism.
Batch and state sizes are bounded, so the ledger cannot grow without limit.
A scan that reaches its bound is not falsely completed.

gates.limitations: Unsigned swift test process on the macos-latest runner, OS and Xcode versions unrecorded. Quota pressure is created by writing small payloads against reduced test bounds rather than by filling the real limits, and the stores are temporary directories standing in for the App Group container. Disk exhaustion itself is never produced.

gates.normative_summary: A known failed, unsupported or zero-text digest. Repeated events and the 15-minute and 24-hour checks do not repeat processing and do not show success.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion watching a member whose last outcome was a known negative.

evidence.covers: An unchanged digest completes the claim without publishing again.
The two intervals the gate names are the scheduler's pinned intervals.
An unsupported format never qualifies, so it is not re-attempted as a candidate.
An empty file is unsupported rather than a zero-text success.

An unsupported-format failure and a zero-text failure recorded on the queue leave the watch unprocessed across three repeated event passes and across both the 15-minute and the 24-hour check driven on the real scheduler and executor, with the queue byte-identical throughout and no successful capture shown for the new bytes.

gates.limitations: Both intervals are driven on the real FolderReconciliationScheduler and FolderReconciliationExecutor through the reconciliationClock seam rather than merely pinned as constants, and a control case shows an ordinary watch still being scheduled. The suppression is watch-wide: a failed outcome puts the whole watch in review and clears the member's observed digest, rather than remembering the negative per digest, so what happens to the same bytes after a person resumes the watch is outside this evidence. The two failure codes are written onto the production queue by the test rather than arriving from a Core receipt, and no production logic distinguishes one from the other. The grant is a stub bookmark codec.

gates.normative_summary: A new parser or profile. New captures use the approved profile, and old retained sources and the excluded baseline are not mass reprocessed.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion plus the Core extraction profile boundary, across a profile change.

evidence.covers: A changed profile is an idempotency conflict and runs no extraction, so nothing is silently reprocessed.
The selection reaches an immutable profile, so new captures bind the approved one.
A legacy ledger is frozen across updates rather than re-enrolled.

gates.missing_condition: No test introduces a new parser or profile version and then shows that retained sources and baseline-excluded members are left alone. The no-mass-reprocess requirement is the gate's subject and has no assertion; the profile-conflict refusal covers a single explicit reprocess request instead.
gates.limitations: Profile immutability and the per-request conflict are covered directly. Behaviour across a version change at population scale is not covered on either side.

gates.normative_summary: Canonical retention and deletion. Unchanged removed contents are not reconstructed, and suppression survives overlap, rename, restart and the daily checks.
gates.applicability: The Core retention boundary plus the companion overlap and scheduling stores.

evidence.covers: Retention only moves forward, so removed content is never reconstructed as current.
A removed source keeps refusing extractions however often it is offered.
Generations keep rising across restarts, so a suppressed generation cannot recur.

gates.missing_condition: Suppression is not shown surviving the four conditions the gate names. No test carries a suppressed source through an overlapping root, a rename, a restart and a daily check; the Core refusals are proven in one process without any of those events.
gates.limitations: The no-reconstruction half is covered on the Core side and is sound. The durability-of-suppression half, which is why this gate is distinct from MON-25, is not covered.

gates.normative_summary: Reverse job completion and a stale base. Old snapshots remain historical, and no changed base or later admission silently wins head eligibility.
gates.applicability: The Core canonical head-ordering boundary on every OS the runtime supports.

evidence.covers: Reverse completion leaves the newer head standing.
A stale base stays historical and never wins head eligibility.
A later admission is told it is no longer the head rather than silently winning.
A reprocess against a stale expected head is historical.

gates.limitations: Core side only, single process, real SQLite store. Completion order is chosen by each test rather than genuinely raced across workers, so the invariants hold over commit sequence rather than under concurrent contention. No companion queue supplies the snapshots and no automatic scheduler drives the jobs.

gates.normative_summary: An add or change burst threshold. At 100 in five minutes the scope pauses new automatic reads and publications, and an approved backfill exemption is exact.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion watching a folder that grows unusually fast.

evidence.covers: Unusual growth requires explicit review before any automatic read or publication.
The paused scope schedules no automatic metadata or content read.

gates.missing_condition: Neither the 100-item count nor the five-minute window is asserted anywhere, so the threshold the gate specifies is not pinned by a test. The approved backfill exemption is not covered at all, so nothing shows it being exact rather than a blanket resumption.
gates.limitations: The pause-on-unusual-growth behaviour is covered, which is the right mechanism. Its trigger values and its exemption are the gate's substance and have no assertions.

gates.normative_summary: A disappearance threshold. Both the 20-item and 10 per cent conditions are required after complete coverage, and a remount failure or a partial scan does not trigger a false deletion.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion watching a folder whose members disappear in bulk.

evidence.covers: An unusual disappearance requires review before members are marked absent.
A partial scan does not touch the prior inventory, so it cannot cause a false deletion.
An unavailable provider must report that nothing was covered, so a remount failure is not absence.
An unlistable root is not reported as an empty folder.

gates.missing_condition: Neither threshold value is asserted. No test shows that both the 20-item and the 10 per cent conditions must hold together, nor that the complete-coverage precondition gates them, so the conjunction the gate specifies is unproven.
gates.limitations: The no-false-deletion half is covered unusually well across three different layers. The threshold conjunction, which is the other half, has no coverage.

gates.normative_summary: Scan and recursion limits. An incomplete scope is visible, and there is no arbitrary-prefix ingestion and no mass absence inference.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion scope policy and reconciliation executor on every watched root.

evidence.covers: A subtree that fails partway leaves the scan visibly incomplete.
Incomplete coverage is reported to the person as counts, so it is visible without disclosing paths.
Containment is component bounded, which is exactly the no-arbitrary-prefix requirement.
A scan reaching its bound is reported as not finished.
The examined-entry bound is likewise reported as an unfinished pass.
A partial scan touches no inventory, which is the no-mass-absence-inference requirement.
Depth beyond the reviewed recursion limit is excluded.

gates.limitations: Unsigned swift test process on the macos-latest runner, OS and Xcode versions unrecorded. Bounds are exercised against reduced test limits over small temporary trees rather than at the shipped limits over a large real tree, so the reporting is proven while the limit values themselves are only pinned as the reviewed design bounds in a separate test.

gates.normative_summary: An unusual review, then more changes. The approval is bound to the reviewed inventory and configuration, and a materially changed review scope is updated.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion after an unusual-change review, when further changes arrive.

evidence.covers: A rejected folder update requires review and can be retried, which is the review binding.
An acknowledgement is scoped to the same subscription, configuration and epoch it was made for.
A configuration generation that moved on is stale, so an approval cannot outlive its configuration.

gates.missing_condition: No test performs an unusual-change review and then delivers further changes to show the reviewed inventory being updated when the scope has materially changed. The generation staleness rules exist and are covered, but nothing binds an approval to a specific reviewed inventory.
gates.limitations: Configuration and epoch scoping are covered precisely at the ledger. The review inventory itself is not a tested subject, so neither clause of the required result is demonstrated on its own terms.

gates.normative_summary: Signed update, downgrade and uninstall. A stable grant owner, a preserved queue and subscription schema and no duplicate watcher, with unknown schemas preserved and original files untouched.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later across a signed update, a rollback and an uninstall of the companion.

evidence.covers: The grant owner stays stable across an update rather than being re-derived.
An unknown newer schema is preserved exactly rather than rewritten.
One observation ledger per environment, which is the no-duplicate-watcher rule.
Original bytes and attributes are unchanged by the companion's own reads.

gates.missing_condition: No signed build exists to update, roll back or uninstall, and no installer owns those operations. Grant-owner stability across a reinstall additionally depends on real security-scoped bookmarks, which every test stubs to a path string.
gates.limitations: Schema preservation and the single-watcher invariant are covered thoroughly within one process. The three lifecycle events the gate names are each simulated by writing a document with a different version number or by reopening a store.

gates.normative_summary: Add with Keep updated while the initial association or activation is interrupted. The initial capture and the pending subscription retain their identities, no background reads occur before confirmed canonical activation, and there is no late reactivation after a local stop.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion establishing a watch alongside a first capture, across an interruption.

evidence.covers: An interruption right after the intent and root write orphans nothing and recovers in full, so identities are retained.
An interruption before activation holds both owners without granting discovery, which is the no-background-reads requirement.
An interruption after activation retires the intent without repeating the work.
Nothing is read or queued before the baseline is canonically admitted.
A pending establishment is finished before a new submission counts watches, so a partial state is not double-counted.

gates.missing_condition: The no-late-reactivation-after-a-local-stop clause is not covered. No test stops a watch locally while its activation is still pending and then shows the late canonical confirmation failing to reactivate it, which is the one-way-door this gate requires.
gates.limitations: Crash-safe establishment is covered at every modelled boundary and is strong. The interruptions are store-level rather than real process kills, Core admission is a fake, and the bookmark codec is stubbed.

gates.normative_summary: A profile or language resource update during queued or active work. The pending input, profile and resource digest are unchanged, and exact worker resources are retained or the operation pauses, never substituted beneath its key. A full 512 MiB managed cache evicts only unpinned resources or defers installation and new-profile admission; pinned resources and the cap remain intact.
gates.applicability: The Core document worker and its managed OCR resource store on every OS the runtime supports.

evidence.covers: The capacity constant the gate names is pinned at exactly 512 MiB.
Pin bookkeeping refuses duplicates, which is the record that would protect a resource from eviction.
One operation may pin two resource sets, so a pending job can retain everything it needs.
A resource whose bytes do not match its digest is never invoked, so nothing is substituted beneath its key.
A text-only profile pins nothing, which bounds what the pin set means.
An install into a full cache evicts another language's unpinned resource to fit, names what it evicted and deletes its directory.
Across every install order, the victims are the shortest prefix of the cache's own stable-key order that covers the shortfall.
A pinned resource is never a victim: the install is refused with language_storage_full and the pin survives.
A leased resource is never a victim either, so a running extraction cannot lose its bytes to an install.
A resource whose bytes fail verification is neither evicted nor counted as reclaimable room.
When eviction cannot free enough, the installation is deferred with the capacity it needed, the pins stay held and the accounted bytes stay at or under the cap.
A capacity deferral leaves the state document byte-for-byte unchanged, so nothing is spent on a refusal.
The cap the eviction and deferral arithmetic runs against is the design's 512 MiB.
Two concurrent processes racing for the same room cannot both spend it: the one eviction cannot absorb defers, and the pinned entry and the cap both survive.
A newer model revision installed while a capture is queued never reaches it: the frozen profile keeps the admitted model hashes and its digest is unchanged.
A language-preference change and a model change together leave the queued capture's admitted profile digest alone.
A queued capture whose pin was lost pauses rather than re-pinning, which is the pauses-rather-than-substitutes half.
During active work the resolved selection is held: a removal attempted mid-extraction is refused as pinned and reconciliation changes nothing.

gates.missing_condition: Two conditions remain. New-profile admission is never deferred for capacity: language_storage_full is raised only inside the resource lifecycle, and no admission path maps it, so a new profile meeting a full cache is refused for a resource that is not installed rather than deferred until room exists. And no test asserts the pending input itself is unchanged across a profile or resource update -- the in-flight evidence pins the frozen profile, its model hashes and its digest, not the queued bytes.
gates.limitations: Eviction, its three exclusions -- pinned, leased and unverified -- the shortest-prefix victim order, the capacity deferral, and the intactness of both the pins and the cap are each covered against the production lifecycle, including across two processes. Profile and language-resource updates during queued and active work are covered over a real capture runner. The 512 MiB figure is pinned as a constant and the arithmetic reached by writing a large byte_size into the state: every eviction test shrinks the capacity, because evicting against a real 512 MiB cache would mean writing 512 MiB. Model payloads are stand-in bytes pinned by their real digests, not Tesseract data. No test combines a real admission pin with an install that would need eviction. The in-flight evidence lives in a module that imports Pillow at import time, so it needs the declared raster dependencies present to collect at all.

gates.normative_summary: A new source capture races reprocessing of an older capture. The independent source and extraction heads remain correct, and reprocessing an old source cannot make that old source current.
gates.applicability: The Core canonical source and extraction head boundary on every OS the runtime supports.

evidence.covers: The source and extraction heads cannot move in one write, which is what keeps them independent.
Work against an older base stays historical and never becomes current.
A completion arriving after a newer one is superseded rather than winning.
Reprocessing against a stale expected head is historical, so the old source cannot be made current through it.
A legitimate reprocess publishes from retained bytes, which is the case the refusals must not break.

gates.limitations: Core side only, in a single process against the real SQLite store and ServiceRunner. The race is sequenced deterministically by each test rather than run concurrently, so the head invariants are proven over commit order and not under genuine contention between a capture and a reprocess worker. No companion or scheduler participates.

gates.normative_summary: Mixed ordinary files and multiple folder modes. Each reviewed group has its own confirmation and receipt, and one group cannot silently submit another or claim whole-collection atomicity.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion review draft holding ordinary files alongside more than one folder group.

evidence.covers: Each group is confirmed and receipted independently, in any order.
Confirming one folder never submits the pending files or the other folder.
Confirming the files never submits a pending folder.
One failed group does not fail or cancel the others, which refutes whole-collection atomicity.
Cancelling one folder is reported for that folder alone.
A restart keeps each confirmed group durable and restores only the unconfirmed ones.
A folder is never published with, or blocking, the ordinary files beside it.

gates.limitations: Unsigned swift test process on the macos-latest runner, OS and Xcode versions unrecorded. Groups are assembled in-test rather than arriving from real pickers, drops or extensions, the delivery client is a fake, and the restart is a store reopen rather than a process relaunch. The receipts are checked as records, not as rendered UI.

gates.normative_summary: Upgrade from v1 native access and the v2 mailbox, then downgrade. Original requests preserve their exact canonical request and keys and acquire no watch consent, and unknown full-solution schemas are preserved and blocked.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion across a forward migration of the access store and the handoff mailbox, and a subsequent rollback.

evidence.covers: The v1 per-member access layout migrates forward to one root grant.
A contradictory legacy record fails closed rather than being resolved by guesswork.
A v1 interrupted attempt migrates without inventing a new identity, which preserves the exact request and keys.
An unknown newer schema is blocked and its bytes are preserved.
A prior v1 publication is recovered as an explicitly legacy unresolved intent rather than being reinterpreted.

gates.missing_condition: No test performs a downgrade after the upgrade, so the round trip the gate names is never exercised. No test asserts that a migrated v1 access record acquires no watch consent either, which is the gate's one substantive behavioural clause beyond schema handling.
gates.limitations: Forward migration and unknown-schema preservation are covered thoroughly at every store. Both are proven by writing a legacy or future document and reopening it, with no build change and no second component version involved.

gates.normative_summary: Full prototype and native handoff coverage. Every complete-solution capability maps to a real implementation package and to acceptance evidence, and simulated UI results are clearly separated from native, Core and parser proof.
gates.applicability: The whole complete-solution capability set. This is the meta-gate WP-15 itself answers, and this ledger is the artefact that answers it.

evidence.covers: The mapping itself: every gate in section 20 with its applicability, its evidence class, its repository evidence, a result and the exact condition still missing.
The closed schema that keeps the mapping's shape, its status vocabulary and its evidence vocabulary from drifting.
The deterministic gate that rejects a missing or duplicate gate, an unknown status, a stale or nonexistent evidence reference, and a passed gate without supporting evidence.
The fail-closed proof that the checker rejects each of those defects rather than passing by accident.
The human-readable status generated from the ledger, with counts by family and by status.

gates.missing_condition: The mapping this gate requires now exists and is enforced, but the gate requires every capability to map to acceptance evidence, and most gates in this ledger do not have it. The separation clause is also only partly met: the evidence_type vocabulary separates repository tests from installed-build, real-host, accessibility and external-fixture evidence, but no simulated UI or prototype result is recorded anywhere, so there is nothing yet to separate on that axis.
gates.limitations: This gate cannot be met by its own artefact. The ledger makes the coverage auditable and makes a false claim of qualification fail the build; it does not itself constitute the acceptance evidence the other 129 gates need.
